incidents_logged: During the unloading of materials, the worker attempted to lift a load that had a slippery surface due to the presence of electrical meterials. The load slipped from the worker’s hands, resulting in loss of control and causing injury to the finger

The incident occurred due to unsafe handling of electrical materials during unloading, where the load had slippery or poorly packed surfaces, leading to loss of grip and control. This was further caused by lack of proper PPE (such as anti-slip gloves)techniques.

Correct Action :Stopped unloading activity immediately after the incident

Provided first aid to the injured person

Inspected the electrical materials

Removed unsafe materials from the work area

Ensured proper PPE (gloves) was used before restarting work

Briefed workers on the incident and immediate safety precautions

Preventive Action:

Toolbox talks before starting unloading activities

Provide appropriate PPE for all workers involved in unloading

Conduct regular safety training on material handling

Ensure proper stacking and storage of electrical materials

Assign supervisor during unloading operations

incidents_logged: Minor left leg injury caused by a brick falling during unloading
While shifting bricks from one place to another place manually . The worker lost balance and a brick felt down on to their neck. This resulted in a minor injury to the neck area

1st Case: The worker slipped on a wet surface caused by water accumulation and substant an injury to the hand while attempting to break the fall 2nd Case: A brick accidentally fell onto the worker leg finger during work activities, causing pain and minor swelling.
The worker was carried out electrical work using step Ladder. During the activity the worker experienced a minor hand injury and a small leg injury. No fall from height occurred.

1.Failure to follow safe step ladder work practices.

2.Insufficient attention to maintaining proper balance and body positioning during the activity.

Correct Action:

1.Provided first aid to the injured worker.

2.Stopped the work and inspected the step ladder for any defects.

3.Briefed the worker on the correct and safe method of using a step ladder.

4.Verified that the worker was fit to resume work before restarting the activity.

Preventive Action:

1.Conduct a pre-job risk assessment before electrical work.

2.Ensure workers maintain three-point contact while using step ladders.

3.Conduct regular toolbox talks on ladder safety and safe working practices.

4.Ensure workers wear appropriate PPE, including safety gloves and safety shoes.

5.Provide regular supervision to ensure compliance with safe work procedures.

1st Case: During the unloading of pipes, one of the pipes accidentally slipped and fell onto the worker’s foot, causing a minor injury to his toe. First aid was provided immediately, and the worker was advised to take necessary medical attention.

2nd Case:A worker sustained a minor cut injury to his hand while carrying out chipping activity. The injury occurred due to contact with the chipping tool/material during the work.

1st Case:The pipe was not properly secured during the unloading activity, causing it to slip unexpectedly. Inadequate control of the pipe and improper handling/unloading practices led to the worker’s foot being positioned within the potential drop zone

2nd Case:The worker’s hand came into contact with the chipping tool/material due to improper hand positioning and inadequate control of the tool during the chipping activity. Insufficient attention to safe working practices and PPE compliance contributed to the minor hand injury.

1st Case CAPA :The injured worker was given first aid and advised to take rest. The unloading activity was temporarily stopped, and the workers were briefed on safe pipe-handling and unloading procedures. Proper lifting and handling methods were reinforced to prevent recurrence.

  • conduct a toolbox talk on safe pipe unloading and manual handling procedures.
  • Ensure pipes are properly secured and stable before unloading.
  • Maintain a safe distance between workers and suspended or moving pipes.

2nd Case: The worker was provided first aid, and the chipping activity was temporarily stopped. The work area and tools were inspected, and the worker was briefed on safe chipping practices.

  • Conduct a toolbox talk on safe chipping practices
  • Ensure proper hand gloves and other required PPE are worn
  • Maintain proper hand positioning while using chipping tools
  • Ensure adequate supervision during chipping activities.

incidents_logged:
NEAR MISS-1

During loading activity time shuttering plate loading into trailer with damaged web sling occurs upside during works may falling into workmen.


NEAR MISS-2

During rainy whether time excavated soil near the road became wet and slippery due to water accumulation and reduced the soil stability mud skid conditions

NEAR MISS-1

  1. Lack of pre-use inspection of lifting accessories.
  2. Improper storage and maintenance of web sling.
  3. Inadequate monitoring for loading activity works


NEAR MISS-2

  1. Excavation soil was stored too close to the live traffic lane
  2. Inadequate planning for rainy weather conditions
  3. Inadequate supervision in work place.﻿

NEAR MISS-1

  1. Remove the damaged web sling with a certified , inspected web sling of the correct safe working load
  2. Periodic inspections for lifting activity works
  3. Store web slings properly in a clean.


NEAR MISS-2

  1. Remove mud and wet soil from the road immediately
  2. Deploy Housekeeping persons to continuously clean the road during and after rainfall.
  3. Don't stock the soil excavated soil adjacent during the rainy season to prevent wash-off

incidents_logged: While flooring leveling work was in progress at MLA Quarters near the 6th Tower ground floor, loose brick material placed on the podium wall suddenly fell adjacent to the workmen. The falling material landed near the workers, creating a potential risk of injury. No personnel were injured and no property damage occurred.

Ø Loose brick materials were improperly stacked/placed on the podium wall.

Ø Lack of proper securing /edge protection to prevent materials from falling.

1.Immediately stopped the ongoing flooring leveling work in the affected area.

2.Inspected the podium wall and identified loose brick materials.

3.Ensured all loose materials were safely removed and secured.

4.Instructed workers to clear the fall zone and maintain safe distance.

5.Informed the site engineer and safety team about the near miss incident.

6.Conducted a brief toolbox talk on falling object hazards and safe material storage.

7. Ensured housekeeping and safety measures were improved before resuming work.

8.Ensure no loose materials are stored on podium walls or at height without proper securing.

9.Implement strict housekeeping practices in all work areas.

10.Provide proper barricading and warning signage near podium walls and edge zones.

11.Conduct regular inspections before starting any activity near elevated structures.

12.Include falling object hazards in daily toolbox talks.

13.Assign responsibility for safe material storage and periodic checks.

14.Use toe boards or netting where there is a risk of falling materials.

incidents_logged: During granite shifting operations from the ground floor to the second floor using a monkey hoist with the help of a web sling, the sling was not properly tightened and slipped unexpectedly, causing the granite to fall to the ground. No injuries to personnel or damage to property were observed.

1. Work was stopped immediately.

2. The web sling was inspected and replaced if required.

3. Workers were instructed to ensure proper securing of loads before lifting.

4. Proper tightening and safe lifting practices were explained to workers.

5. A toolbox talk was conducted focusing on lifting safety and proper use of slings.

Assign a trained and competent person to supervise all lifting operations.

1.      Ensure proper selection and use of certified lifting slings for the load.

2.  Always verify correct tightening and securing of slings before lifting.

3. Conduct pre-use inspection of all lifting tools and accessories.

4.  Assign a trained and competent person to supervise lifting operations.

5.  Provide proper training to workers on safe lifting techniques.

6.  Use tag lines to control load movement during lifting.

Ensure effective communication between workers during lifting activities
No Near miss cases recorded in the month of April-2026

On 08.02.2026, Power Duct Wall 2nd lift concreting work was in progress by the workmen of M/s Navayuga Infra. As the concreting location was not directly accessible through chute concreting, a boom placer was deployed for carrying out the concreting activity.


During the concreting operation, Mr. Samir Pramanick (Fitter, 37 years) was holding the elephant hose while standing on a 1.2-meter-high wall. Due to sudden jerks during pumping, the concrete block placed beneath the boom placer outrigger broke, causing slight inclination of the boom placer. As a result of the sudden tilt, Mr. Samir Pramanick lost his balance and fell to the ground. Fortunately, no injuries were reported.

1. Improper outrigger base support – The concrete block used beneath the outrigger was inadequate and not to withstand the operational load.


2. Unsafe work positioning – The worker was standing on a 1.2-meter-high wall without proper working platform.


3. Lack of proper supervision before starting boom placer operation.


4. Sudden pressure jerks in the pumping line without adequate control measures.1. Improper outrigger base support – The concrete block used beneath the outrigger was inadequate and not to withstand the operational load.

1. Work was immediately stopped after the incident.


2. Boom placer stability was checked and re-leveled properly.


3. Damaged concrete block was removed and replaced with adequate load-bearing capacity.


4. Tool box talk conducted with all workers regarding safe handling of the elephant hose and safe working at height.


5. Reinforcement of supervision during concreting activities.

incidents_logged: On 23.03.2026 at 11:37 AM, an unauthorized entry was made by an M/s. L&T Transit Mixer (Reg No. AP 39 UV 1690) into the N-12 CH:3+300 site premises for retaining wall concreting work without prior permission. Due to an unknown route, the driver took a turn in the girder casting area. While turning, the rear-end chute came into contact with the girder reinforcement, disturbing the alignment of the steel that had been tied the previous evening. No injuries were reported, as no work activity was in progress during the night shift. Security personnel reported the incident to the Deputy Project Manager and stopped the transit mixer until his arrival for further investigation.

• Entering into unauthorized work zone without prior permission.

• The driver was not properly informed about the correct location and route to the site.

• Absence of guidance personnel-- No traffic marshal or supervisor was available to direct the vehicle.

• Lack of sufficient place for vehicle movement.

• Implement a strict entry permission system for all vehicles entering the site.

• Train security personnel to control and guide vehicle movement effectively.

• Install directional signboards and warning signs at all critical locations.

• Conduct regular safety inspections and monitoring of site access control.

On 15.04.2026, M/s MD Fittu gang was engaged in steel shifting works for concreting and PCC activities. During the manual shifting of a steel channel measuring 150 mm in width and 6 meters in length, a crew of four helpers was involved in the activity. While unloading the channel, due to miscommunication among the helpers, three workers released the channel simultaneously while Mr. Farook Sheik was still supporting it on his shoulder. As a result, he sustained a scratch injury and shoulder muscle swelling due to the sudden load of the full-length channel.


The injured person was immediately shifted to the First Aid Center, where the wound was cleaned and dressed with a minor bandage. No major complications were observed, and the injury was classified as a minor injury.

1. Proper coordination was not maintained among the four helpers during unloading of the steel channel.

2. Three helpers released the channel simultaneously while Mr. Farook Sheik was still supporting the load on his shoulder.

3. No single person was assigned to give clear lifting / lowering commands during the manual shifting activity.

1. The injured person was immediately shifted to the First Aid Center for treatment.

2. The wound was cleaned and dressed, and first aid was provided for shoulder muscle swelling.

3. The steel shifting activity was resumed only after proper briefing and supervision.

4. A toolbox talk was conducted on team lifting, communication, and safe load handling practices.

On 24.06.2026 at 05:17 PM, a Hydra Crane (Reg. No. AP40 FU 4904) unloaded DI pipes from a trailer and commenced its return journey to the camp towards Rayapudi via the E-3 seed access road.

While travelling on the road, the crane encountered a car parked on the two-way carriageway. After approaching the parked car, the crane operator brought the vehicle to a slow stop and then carefully proceeded to pass the parked car while negotiating a curve. At the same time, a private bus approached from the opposite direction without stopping or allowing sufficient clearance. During the manoeuvre, the edge of the Hydra crane came into contact with the rear end of the private bus, resulting in a crack on the rear emergency exit window.

No injuries or casualties were reported in the incident.

·      Contact occurred while the Hydra crane was negotiating a curve to pass a parked vehicle.

·      The private bus continued approaching without stopping or maintaining adequate clearance.

·      Car parked on the two-way access road, reducing the available carriageway width.

·       Implement a comprehensive Traffic Management Plan covering all construction access roads.

·       Designate separate entry and exit routes for heavy vehicles wherever feasible.

·       Ensure heavy vehicles use spotters while negotiating blind curves or narrow passages.

·       Conduct periodic defensive driving and road safety awareness training.

·       Carry out routine inspections of access roads to identify and eliminate traffic hazards.

·       Schedule heavy vehicle movement during periods of lower traffic density whenever practicable.

incidents_logged:
On 17.07.2026 at 09:34 AM, a Hydra Crane (Reg. No. AP40 FU 4904) was engaged in loading 16 mm reinforcement steel bundles onto a trailer for transportation to the Power Duct work location at CH:5+800. While lifting the steel bundle using two (02) 10-ton web slings, the load became tilted due to improper load distribution during lifting. As a result, the tilted rebar bundle came into contact with the Hydra crane pulley, causing the wire rope to slip out of the pulley groove.

The crane operator immediately stopped the lifting operation and safely lowered the steel bundle to the ground. The web slings were removed, and the wire rope was correctly repositioned in the pulley groove before resuming the operation. No injury to personnel, equipment damage, or material damage was reported. The incident was classified as a Near Miss.

1. The rebar bundle tilted because the load was not evenly distributed between the two web slings.
  2. The tilted load came into contact with the crane pulley, causing the wire rope to slip out of the pulley groove.
  3. Inadequate verification of the load's center of gravity.

1. Prepare and follow a lifting plan for all heavy and critical lifting activities.
  2. Ensure proper sling selection, sling angle, and load balancing based on the load's centre of gravity.
  3. Conduct a trial lift (100–200 mm above ground) to verify load stability before proceeding with the full lift.
  4. Ensure lifting operations are supervised by a competent Lifting Supervisor, Rigger, and Banksman.
  5. Inspect cranes, wire ropes, pulleys, shackles, and web slings before each lifting operation.
  6. Barricade the lifting area and prohibit personnel from entering the suspended load zone.
  7. Conduct periodic training and toolbox talks on safe lifting practices, rigging techniques, and emergency response during lifting operations.
5. Hydra Crane Near Miss Report N12 17.07.2026.pdf

incidents_logged:
During soil shifting activity, a loaded tipper vehicle was transporting excavated soil through the designated haul road. It was observed that the vehicle tilted toward one side while moving on an uneven and soft road surface. The unsafe road condition and side slope created a potential risk of vehicle rollover.

 

The driver immediately stopped the vehicle after noticing the instability and concerned engineer. The work area was inspected, and the unsafe condition was identified. No injury, property damage, equipment damage, or environmental impact occurred.

 

The incident is classified as a Near Miss due to the potential risk of vehicle overturning caused by unstable haul road conditions.

·        Uneven haul road condition.

·        Soft and loose ground surface.

·        Presence of side slope on vehicle route.

·        Inadequate road maintenance.

·        Lack of routine road condition inspection.

·        Daily haul road inspection checklist implementation.

·        Regular grading and compaction of haul roads.

·        Mandatory reporting of unsafe road conditions.

·        Installation of warning signboards at critical locations.

·        Monthly defensive driving and safety awareness training.

·        Weekly HSE inspection and compliance review.

During rebar cutting work, the cutting wheel suddenly broke while the machine was running.

The broken pieces fell and scattered around the nearby area.

The operator stopped the work immediately after the incident.

No one was injured during the event.

There was no damage to any property or equipment.

·      Defective or Damaged Wheel

·      Improper Usage / Excessive Force

·      Incorrect Wheel Selection

·      Inadequate Training / Awareness


Improper Installation

Corrective Action taken:

·      Ensure all cutting wheels are inspected before use (check for cracks, defects)

·      Use only manufacturer-approved wheels compatible with the machine

·      Verify correct installation and secure mounting

·      Train operators on proper cutting techniques (avoid excessive force)

·      Replace worn or expired wheels immediately

Preventive Action:

·      Conduct refresher training on safe tool handling

·      Enforce use of appropriate PPE (safety goggles, face shield, gloves)

·      Store cutting wheels properly to prevent damage (dry, flat, protected area)

·      Ensure machine guards are properly installed and in place

incidents_logged: During a routine site inspection, the temporary sheet fencing was found tilted towards one side due to instability. The unsafe condition was identified before the fencing collapsed. Fortunately, no person was injured and no property damage occurred. The area was immediately secured, and corrective action was initiated

The temporary fencing lost its stability and tilted to one side.

· The supporting posts/base were found to be inadequately secured.

· Strong wind, loose foundation, or ground settlement may have contributed to the instability.

· Routine inspection did not identify the weakening of the fencing support in time.


· The fencing had not been adequately reinforced with additional bracing.

Corrective Action taken:

· Reinstall and properly anchor the fencing posts.

· Provide additional bracing/support to improve stability.

· Replace any damaged fencing panels and supports.

· Inspect the entire fencing line for similar defects.

Preventive Action:

· Conduct daily inspections of all temporary fencing.

· Ensure fencing is properly anchored and braced during installation.

· Inspect fencing after heavy rain, strong winds, or ground disturbance.

incidents_logged: During material shifting activities, the worker’s foot slipped, causing him to fall on the ground and sustain minor injuries. He was immediately taken to SPCPL centre for First-aid treatment after the fist-aid he is resume his duty

1.Inadequate housekeeping in the work area .

2.Presence of slippery or uneven surface at the material shifting location.

Corrective Actions (Immediate):

1. First aid was provided immediately to the injured person, and proper dressing was done.

2. The injured worker was sent to the medical facility for further check-up.

3. Work was stopped temporarily at the location to assess the situation.

4. The involved tools and work method were inspected to identify the cause of the steel slipping.

5. Unsafe conditions were corrected before resuming the activity.

6. A toolbox talk was conducted with workers to highlight the incident and immediate precautions.

Preventive Actions (Future Control Measures):

1. Ensure proper clamping or securing of steel materials before cutting to prevent slipping.

2. Provide and enforce the use of appropriate PPE, including cut-resistant gloves and safety shoes.

3. Use proper tools such as vices, clamps, or supports during cutting operations.

3. Avoid manual holding of steel while cutting; ensure stable positioning at all times.

4. Conduct regular inspection and maintenance of cutting tools and equipment.

5. Provide proper training to workers on safe cutting practices and hazard awareness.

6. Ensure adequate supervision during high-risk activities like cutting and grinding.

7. Maintain good housekeeping to avoid obstruction and ensure safe working posture.

On 1st April a 75-ton crane (Amaravati Crane) was attempting to move up the ramp at the Tower-2 entrance (North-East corner). During the maneuver, the crane was unable to climb the ramp due to inadequate traction and improper operational judgment/calculation by the operator. As a result, the vehicle lost stability and rolled backward unexpectedly.During the reverse movement, the crane collided with a shuttering board positioned behind the vehicle. The impact caused the shuttering board to skid and strike the upper toe area of a workman’s left foot while he was standing behind the board.The injured worker was immediately shifted to the site first-aid center for initial treatment and was subsequently referred to the hospital for detailed medical examination. Medical evaluation and scanning confirmed a hairline fracture in the third toe bone of the left foot.

Immediate Causes

  1. Crane lost traction while moving upward on the ramp.
  2. Uncontrolled backward movement of the crane.
  3. Presence of unsecured shuttering material in the crane movement path.
  4. Worker positioned within the danger zone behind the shuttering board.

Contributing Causes

  1. Inadequate assessment of ramp gradient and traction condition before crane movement.
  2. Improper operational judgment/planning by the crane operator.
  3. Absence of effective wheel chocking or anti-rollback control during ramp movement.
  4. Poor barricading and segregation of personnel from equipment movement areas.
  5. Improper material storage/placement near the access route.
  6. Inadequate banks-man control during crane maneuvering on the ramp..

Root Causes

  1. Failure in planning and risk assessment for heavy equipment movement on inclined surfaces.
  2. Insufficient supervision and monitoring of crane operation activities.
  3. Deficient housekeeping and material management near operational access routes.

Corrective Actions

  1. Stop crane movement activity immediately and secure the area.
  2. Remove all loose shuttering boards and obstructions from crane movement paths.
  3. Conduct inspection of ramp condition, gradient, and traction suitability before resuming operations.
  4. Re-brief crane operators, banks-men, and workers on safe movement procedures and exclusion zones.
  5. Ensure wheel chocks and anti-rollback measures are available and used during incline operations.
  6. Barricade and restrict unauthorized personnel from equipment operating zones.

Preventive Actions


  1. Conduct pre-movement route surveys for all heavy equipment operations.
  2. Install anti-skid/traction improvement measures on ramps where required.
  3. Deploy trained banks-men for all critical crane movements.
  4. Establish clearly marked exclusion zones during equipment movement.
  5. Implement proper material stacking and housekeeping controls near access roads and ramps.
  6. Conduct competency assessment and refresher training for crane operators on gradient/ramp operations.
  7. Introduce supervisory approval before moving heavy equipment on inclined paths.
  8. Periodically audit crane movement practices and compliance with safety procedures

incidents_logged:
On 02/05/2026 at approximately 05:37 PM, a High Potential Near Miss incident occurred at the northeast side of Tower-1 during the lifting and shifting operation of Meva shuttering (Jump Form) boards using a 250-ton mobile crane.

During the lowering and positioning of the jump form board, the suspended load came into unintended contact with the ladder portion of the diagonal grid column due to inadequate space management and insufficient clearance control during the lifting operation. The unloading area was congested with other shuttering boards and unwanted materials, resulting in limited maneuvering space and causing the load to remain suspended for an extended period during positioning. Consequently, the suspended load unintentionally contacted the ladder portion of the structure.At the time of the incident, the signalman was guiding the crane operator using hand signals, although a walkie-talkie was available but found to be in an off condition, resulting in ineffective communication during the critical lifting activity.

Fortunately, no personnel injury or major property damage was reported. However, the incident had the potential to cause serious injury, structural damage, or a dropped-object incident

1.     Failure to properly plan and prepare the unloading area before commencement of lifting activities.

2.     Deficiency in communication verification and coordination among lifting team members.

3.     Insufficient control measures for lifting operations in restricted and congested work areas.

4.     Inadequate implementation of lifting risk assessment and safe lifting procedures.

5.     Inadequate supervision during critical lifting and positioning activity

1.     The lifting activity was immediately stopped, and the affected area was secured.

2.     All unnecessary materials and obstructing shuttering boards were removed from the unloading area.

3.     The unloading zone was reorganized to ensure sufficient clearance for safe lifting and positioning operations.

4.     The walkie-talkie communication system was checked, restored, and verified before resuming operations.

5.     Crane operator, signalman, riggers, and supervisors were briefed regarding the incident and safe lifting requirements especially on the blind spots and congested areas.

6.     The lifting plan and unloading arrangement were reviewed prior to continuation of the activity.

Dedicated supervision was assigned to monitor load clearance and positioning during lifting operations.

On 09/07/2026 at approximately 06:59 PM, a near miss incident occurred at the NTA Podium 5 area, near the bar cutting machine, during the preparation for column concreting at P2 using a 15 RPM concrete pump.

The concrete pump pipeline routing had been almost completed, and the pipeline was supported on scaffolding at an approximate height of 3 meters. Before confirming that the pipeline joints were properly secured and tightened, the concrete pump operator started operating the pump without obtaining final clearance.

Due to the vibration generated by the pump, an improperly joined and inadequately tightened pipeline connection at the terminal end became disconnected, causing the end portion of the pipeline to fall onto the concreting surface. As a result, concrete splashed and scattered into the surrounding area.

At the time of the incident, another work crew was carrying out activities approximately 10 meters away from the location. Fortunately, no personnel were struck by the falling pipeline or concrete splatter, and no injury or property damage occurred.

1.     Inadequate communication between the pipeline installation crew and the pump operator.

2.     Failure to follow the pre-start inspection/checklist.

3.     Lack of supervision before commencing concrete pumping.

1.     Ensure all pipeline joints and couplings are properly aligned, secured, and tightened before concrete pumping.

2.     Ensure effective communication between the concrete pump operator, supervisor, and pipeline installation crew before commencement.

3.     Obtain final clearance from the site supervisor and safety person before operating the concrete pump.

4.     Conduct and document a pre-start inspection of the complete pumping system.

5.     Establish an exclusion zone beneath and around elevated concrete pipelines.

6.     Secure elevated pipeline sections with suitable supports and secondary restraints wherever required.

7.     Deploy a competent supervisor to verify pipeline stability before authorizing concrete pumping.

On 26-08-2026 at approximately 11:03 AM-T 2 North side area, a shuttering workmen gang of M/s Rohit Kumar Gupta was engaged in Shuttering board wingnut tightening activities along the outer side of the MEVA platform at an approximate height of 40 metres.

During the activity, the hammer accidentally slipped from the hand of one of the workmen and fell from the elevated MEVA platform towards the L0 deck sheet level.

At the time of the occurrence, one person was present near the potential falling/drop zone. Fortunately, the person was not struck by the falling hammer, and no injury or property damage occurred.

1.   Inadequate dropped-object prevention and tool/material securing practices during work at height, coupled with insufficient consideration of prevailing environmental conditions such as high wind during the task.

1.   Immediately stop and review the activity before resuming work at the affected location.

2.   Ensure all hand tools used at height, including hammers, spanners and other portable tools, are fitted with suitable tool lanyards/retention systems.

3.   Strictly prohibit personnel from entering or working below elevated activities where there is a potential for falling objects.

4.   Conduct a task-specific Toolbox Talk covering hand-tool security, dropped-object hazards, exclusion zones and safe working practices at height.

5.   Implement material fall prevention catch nets below the platform areas where feasible.

6.   Supervisors shall conduct pre-task inspections to verify that all tools and materials are properly secured before commencing work.

7.   Always ensure No unsecured tools at height – No person below suspended work.

incidents_logged:
Vehicle No.: AP39X 6316

Date: 26-02-2026

Time: 5:30 PM

Location: NEC 24 Road, Block 5

Incident Description:

On 26-02-2026 at approximately 5:30 PM, the TM vehicle (AP39X 6316) was proceeding towards NEC 24 Road, Block 5. The driver became confused due to improper road diversion and entered the wrong route within the site area.

The road condition was congested and unsuitable for smooth vehicle movement. While attempting a right turn, the road width was insufficient to accommodate the vehicle properly. During the maneuver, the soil at the edge of the road suddenly collapsed, causing the vehicle to topple into a deep excavation.

Improper or unclear road.

Insufficient road width for safe right-turn movement of the TM vehicle.

Unstable soil condition at the road edge near the excavation.

Lack of proper barricading around the deep excavation.

Road width at the turning location widened and leveled for safe vehicle movement.

Excavation edges strengthened and compacted to prevent soil collapse.

Proper barricading and warning tapes installed around deep excavation areas.

Toolbox talk conducted for drivers regarding safe driving and site navigation.

incidents_logged: During lunch hours, Mr. Ismail (contractor helper) was proceeding towards the drinking water area from the restroom. Due to the presence of a sharp object on the ground, he sustained a minor cut injury to his leg. Immediate first aid treatment was provided at site. Area was inspected and unsafe material removed.

1. Poor housekeeping in the walking area
  2. Presence of sharp debris/waste material not removed

Corrective Action :-

﻿

  1. Injured worker was provided first aid treatment immediately at site
  2. Sharp object/debris removed from the accident location
  3. Affected area cleaned and made safe for movement
  4. Conducted immediate inspection of nearby work and walking areas


Preventive Action :-


  1. Implement strict housekeeping practices across all site areas
  2. Establish daily cleaning and inspection schedule
  3. Provide designated waste disposal bins for sharp and scrap materials
  4. Ensure mandatory use of PPE, especially safety shoes for all workers
  5. Conduct regular Toolbox Talks on housekeeping and safe walking practices
  6. Assign responsibility to supervisors for monitoring housekeeping conditions
  7. Display safety signboards in common access and movement areas
  8. Perform periodic safety audits and inspections

incidents_logged: While chopping vegetables, the knife accidentally slipped and caused a minor superficial abrasion on the left ring finger. The injury resulted in mild bleeding and pain, with no swelling observed. First aid was provided, and the injured person was advised to keep the wound clean and monitor for any signs of infection.

• Unsafe hand positioning by keeping fingers too close to the cutting edge during chopping.
  • Lack of proper knife-handling technique and attention while performing the task.

• Provide awareness on safe knife-handling practices to mess helpers.
  • Ensure vegetables are placed securely on a stable cutting surface before cutting.
  • Maintain knives in good condition and inspect them regularly.
  • Consider providing cut-resistant gloves for personnel involved in food preparation activities.

incidents_logged: While handling a steel protruding object, it accidentally struck his right leg between the knee and ankle, resulting in a small linear superficial abrasion with minimal bleeding.

• Immediate Cause: Contact with a protruding steel object while handling materials.
  • Underlying Cause: Inadequate identification and control of protruding/sharp objects in the work area.
  • Contributing Factors: Insufficient housekeeping and lack of proper clearance/arrangement of steel materials.
  • Root Cause: Inadequate workplace inspection and housekeeping controls to identify and eliminate potential contact hazards.

Corrective Actions:

  1. Provided first aid to the injured person and ensured the wound was properly cleaned and dressed.
  2. Removed/secured the protruding steel object from the work area.
  3. Barricaded the affected area until the hazard was completely eliminated.
  4. Instructed workers to maintain safe clearance while handling steel materials.

Preventive Actions:

  1. Conduct regular housekeeping and workplace inspections to identify protruding/sharp objects.
  2. Ensure all steel materials are properly stacked, stored, and secured.
  3. Provide toolbox talks on safe material handling and identification of sharp/protruding hazards.
  4. Ensure appropriate PPE, including safety shoes and gloves, is used during material-handling activities.
  5. HSE team to monitor the area periodically and close similar unsafe conditions immediately.

incidents_logged: During excavation work, localized soil sloughing and partial collapse occurred along the excavation side due to loose and unstable soil. The condition indicated reduced trench-side stability and posed a potential risk of further soil collapse. No personnel were present in the affected area, and no injury, equipment damage, or property damage occurred. The excavation work was immediately stopped and the area was secured for further assessment.

• Immediate Cause: Localized soil sloughing and partial collapse of the excavation side due to loose and unstable soil.
  • Underlying Cause: Inadequate stabilization and protection of the excavation side considering the existing soil condition.
  • Contributing Factors: Insufficient assessment of soil stability and inadequate monitoring of excavation conditions during the work.
  • Root Cause: Inadequate implementation of excavation safety controls, including proper soil stability assessment, excavation profiling, and timely stabilization measures.

Corrective Actions:

  1. Excavation work was immediately stopped and the affected area was secured.
  2. Loose and unstable soil was removed from the excavation side.
  3. The excavation profile was reshaped and stabilized as per the approved excavation methodology.
  4. The excavation area was inspected by a competent person before resuming work.

Preventive Actions:

  1. Conduct soil stability assessment before and during excavation activities.
  2. Provide proper slope, shoring, or other suitable protection based on soil conditions and excavation depth.
  3. Carry out daily excavation inspections and additional inspections after any change in ground conditions.
  4. Conduct TBT on excavation safety, soil collapse hazards, and safe working distances.
  5. Maintain safe access/egress and keep personnel away from unstable excavation edges.
  6. Continuously monitor excavation sides for cracks, sloughing, water seepage, or other signs of instability.

incidents_logged:
On 11 March 2026 at approximately 3:02 PM, a phone call was received from the security guard reporting smoke emerging from the pipe stock yard area. Immediately upon receiving the information, the Emergency Response Team (ERT) rushed to the location to assess the situation.

By the time the team arrived, the fire had already broken out in the Pipe storage area and was spreading uncontrollably. The fire quickly extended to the adjacent pipe stacking area, resulting in damage to the stored materials. Immediate firefighting actions were initiated to control the spread and prevent further damage to nearby assets.

Simultaneously, communication was established with the Fire Department through an emergency phone call. The Fire Department responded promptly, and approximately six fire tenders reached the location to support the firefighting operation. With the combined efforts of the Emergency Response Team and the Fire Department, the fire was brought under control by smothering the fire using spreading of sand with the help of a Backhoe loader and continuous water jet spraying using fire tenders.

 

No injuries have been reported at the time of the incident. The extent of material damage is currently under assessment, and a detailed investigation is being initiated to determine the root cause of the incident.

1. A water tanker with fixed pump arrangement shall be placed in yard to handle emergency situation in case of fire at project site. 
  2. Adequate Fire extinguishers shall be placed based on the fire load calculation at Pipe storage yard.
  3. Combustible materials including grasses shall be removed around the pipe yard and 5M away from fencing to maintain safe workplace at project site.
  4. A peripheral trench shall be excavated, and sand will dump around the project camp area to act as a fire barrier and prevent fire spread.
